title: Book One · Chapter 35: A Little Left
story:
On Sunday, Mum says it is time to put the kite things away properly.

Ronan looks up quickly. Mum points to the loose paper. "We will keep the kite. But we need to put these bits away."

There are more bits than he remembers. Paper under the table. Thread beside his bed. A short strip of bamboo behind the door. Leo comes to help because some of the string is his.

They spread a cloth in the yard. Mum brings the clean empty paste pot. A little dry paste is stuck at the bottom. There is not enough for another kite.

Ronan finds the wet-paper scraps. One piece is flat enough to draw on. Ronan gives it to Leo. Leo draws a big arrow pointing up.

"That can go in our book," Leo says.

They keep one strong bamboo strip for repairs. Dad takes a rough broken end away so nobody steps on it. The cloth tail stays tied to the kite. The string is wound neatly on Leo's card.

"Who keeps that?" Ronan asks.

"The kite stays here," Leo says. "The string can stay with it."

"Is that all right?"

"Yes. I may need it again. Then I will come for it. Ask me first. Then you can cut it."

Ronan nods. Leo wants to keep his own string. Ronan will ask him first.

Mum brings the tea box outside. Ronan counts his own coins. Three. He did not spend these coins on Jun's materials. He did not earn money from the kites either.

"I wanted more coins by now," he says.

"From what?" Leo asks.

"Making things."

"We made one thing."

"And a lot of falling."

Leo gives him a sideways smile. Ronan smiles back. They sit close to look at the page. Neither tells the other to move away. The tea box stays beside them with its three coins.

"How much paper did you use?" Dad asks. They make a rough pile of scraps and a little drawing of the wet sheets. They used many sheets for one finished kite.

"Another kite will need more paper. I may make more mistakes," Ronan says.

"And time," Mum says.

He counts the test marks. Six marks fit on the page. Some tries didn't get marks at all. He writes MORE beside the bottom line, with Mum helping him spell it.

Mrs Lan passes through the gate with her shopping. She stops to admire the clean yard.

"I can see the ground again. A fine new feature."

Mum laughs. Mrs Lan sets down a small bag and asks Ronan for help. "Please carry these two light cloths to my chair," she says. She has both hands full. He does it, and she thanks him.

Ronan waits a moment. No coin appears. Then he feels embarrassed for waiting. He was only carrying cloths from one end of their own yard to the other.

He goes back to the kite. The brown paper has a new crease, but it is dry. Leo checks the knots. Then he leaves.

"Next time we just fly," Leo says.

"Next time we check the wind first."

"And bring water."

They add that to the page. "Do you want to keep all these scraps?" Mum asks. They choose two good pieces and put the rest in the waste bag.

The making corner becomes small again. Ronan closes the tea box. There is a little money left, a little paper left, and a whole kite. The coins go back beside his bed. The paper goes on the board. The kite stays by the door. Each thing has a place now. He can find them easily.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：scraps＝碎片；repairs＝修补；waste＝废弃的东西；coins＝硬币。

理解问题：

1. 风筝做完后，哪些材料还剩下？
2. Ronan 对自己的积蓄和成本有什么更具体的认识？
